articles.title: DOJ asks Supreme Court to allow Trump’s USPS action on mail-in ballots to proceed ahead of midterm elections
articles.excerpt: The appeal came shortly before a federal judge was set to decide whether to issue an injunction blocking requirements dictating how mail-in ballots are sent.
articles.content:
The Trump administration is asking the Supreme Court to green-light a new Postal Service rule that would exert control over mail-in ballots ahead of the midterm elections.

U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani last week issued a temporary restraining order blocking parts of the rule from being implemented.

“With respect to the November 2026 election, the order thus partially nullifies the Postal Service’s efforts to address the risk that the federal mails will be used to perpetrate voter fraud, a particularly pernicious species of fraud that dilutes the votes of lawful voters, prevents election results from reflecting the will of the American people, and undermines ‘public confidence in the integrity of the electoral process,’” Solicitor General D. John Sauer wrote in the application.

While Talwani’s order “allows the Postal Service and the States to continue taking steps to ensure that their envelopes satisfy the rule’s requirements, the order risks sowing confusion and chaos because it makes those preparatory steps voluntary, rather than mandatory,” Sauer wrote.

There is a “grave risk,” Sauer wrote, “that States may not have taken the necessary steps to comply due to the false sense of latitude created by the court’s improper order, potentially depriving those States’ citizens of the ability to vote by mail.”

The filing seeks an immediate stay of Talwani’s order while the case proceeds through the appeals court.

The timing of the request was unexpected, since the administration already had a pending appeal to the 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals and because Talwani was expected to rule Thursday on whether to issue a preliminary injunction.

In her ruling last week, Talwani sided with states and voting rights groups that claimed the rule unlawfully usurped states’ power to regulate their own elections, which would need congressional approval, and left them facing an “impossible” timeline to comply in time for the November elections.

“Through the Final Rule, the USPS is refusing to send mail ballots to eligible voters unless States or local election officials submit their mail ballot envelopes and return envelopes and receive advance approval from the USPS without regard to impending deadlines for the November 3, 2026 election,” she wrote.

It also “requires elections officials to create accounts for a new electronic portal, certify that they have received approval regarding the mail ballot design, and thereafter upload to the USPS portal each voter’s information, including name, address, and a unique intelligent mail barcode,” she noted.

“Based on the record presently before the court, Plaintiff States face irreparable harm where they are required to comply with a likely unconstitutional regulation for which compliance is practically impossible as to the 2026 midterm elections, now little more than two months away,” Talwani wrote.

She said that most states have already ordered their mail ballots and that “some are required by state law to send them to eligible voters as early as next week.” North Carolina is scheduled to begin mailing out ballots Friday.

The states, she added, “have neither time nor funds to design new mail ballots, seek approval of the new designs, order production of mail ballots, update their own election management systems, train election officials to use the USPS portal, and upload citizen data to the portal, all before the midterms.”

While the government has said the measure is necessary to combat voter fraud, Talwani said it had not presented “any evidence regarding fraudulent absentee or mail-in voting.”

The “USPS’s interest in correcting an unsubstantiated problem through likely unconstitutional means is dwarfed by the overwhelming risk of pervasive disenfranchisement of citizens who need access to mail ballots in order to vote,” she wrote.

The rule change came about as the result of an executive order President Donald Trump issued March 31 titled “Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections.”

Talwani had signed off on an earlier order in a related case barring the rule from being implemented, but that ruling was overturned last month by the Supreme Court, which found her decision was premature because the rule had not yet been finalized.

“The court’s disposition of this application does not mean that any measure taken by the Government to implement the order will necessarily be lawful. On that score, time will tell,” the court said in an unsigned 6-3 ruling.

The rule was finalized late last month.

In court filings, the government said the changes that are being implemented are “modest.”

The rule simply turns “longstanding recommendations—which many of the Plaintiff States have already adopted at least in part, and some have long advocated for—into requirements,” the government argued.

It added that “this is ultimately a regulation of the U.S. mail, and a modest one at that—not a federal takeover of election administration by the Postal Service. That basic reality undermines virtually all of Plaintiffs’ claims and illustrates why Defendants are likely to succeed on the merits of their appeal.”

articles.title: Two iPhones, one number: iOS 27 will feature a new Handoff function
articles.excerpt: Apple will introduce a new Handoff feature in iOS 27, which will allow users to share a single phone number across two iPhones. One device will be the primary one and the other the secondary one, and users will be able t
articles.content:
Apple will add a new feature to iOS 27 called Handoff, which will allow users to use two iPhones with the same phone number. One smartphone will be the primary device and the other the secondary one, and users will be able to switch between them without changing their number.

Apple first mentioned this feature at the WWDC 2026 presentation in June, including it in the list of hundreds of iOS 27 innovations. However, the company did not reveal any details at the time. Now, a MacRumors forum member going by the username pdfu has posted a video, in which he demonstrated the feature on two virtual iPhones in Xcode 27.

The primary iPhone will retain the main eSIM, whilst the secondary one will receive a companion eSIM. All mobile network settings will be managed from the primary device, and geolocation will be determined by whichever iPhone is currently being used for calls and mobile data.

The feature can be configured in 'Settings' under the 'Cellular' section. To use it, you'll need two iPhones running iOS 27 and support from your mobile network operator. Among the first operators expected to introduce this capability are T-Mobile in the US and Deutsche Telekom in Germany.

The feature is currently being tested, but its release is expected alongside the final version of iOS 27 later this month.

articles.title: iOS 27 Introduces New 'iPhone Handoff' Feature
articles.excerpt: Apple has added a new "iPhone Handoff" feature to iOS 27 that will allow you to switch between two iPhones while using the same phone number on each device. This functionality was briefly mentioned during the WWDC 2026 k
articles.content:
Apple has added a new "iPhone Handoff" feature to iOS 27 that will allow you to switch between two iPhones while using the same phone number on each device.


This functionality was briefly mentioned during the WWDC 2026 keynote in June, on a slide that listed hundreds of new features coming in iOS 27 and corresponding software updates, but Apple never shared any further details at the time.

MacRumors forum member pdfu today shared a video that demonstrates how the feature will work, using two simulated iPhones running in Xcode 27's Device Hub.

"iPhone Handoff" can be set up from the Settings app, under the Cellular menu. During the setup process, you can choose which iPhone you want to be the main device that you use most often and which one you want to be the companion device.

Apple says a user's main eSIM will remain on the main iPhone, while the companion iPhone will receive a companion eSIM, and this will enable you to switch between the devices back and forth while using the same phone number.

All cellular settings are managed on the main iPhone, and location sharing is based on whichever iPhone is actively using the phone number.

In addition to needing two iPhones running iOS 27, "iPhone Handoff" will seemingly require carrier support. The forum post mentions that T-Mobile in the U.S. and Deutsche Telekom in Germany might be among the first carriers to offer the feature.

Following three months of beta testing, iOS 27 is expected to be released later this month, so we will likely hear more about this feature soon.

京都府舞鶴市の民家でクマが居座り、市が緊急銃猟を実施する準備を進めています。緊急銃猟が行われた場合、京都府内では制度が始まって以来初めてとなります。

舞鶴市によりますと、9月3日午後5時12分、近隣の住民から「クマが縁の下にいる」と警察に通報がありました。警察から連絡を受けた市によりますと、舞鶴市大波下の民家の軒下にツキノワグマが居座っているということです。大きさからクマは親子あわせて2頭いるとみられています。  

クマがいるのは離れの縁の下で、母屋には人がいるということですが、これまでにけが人は出ていません。 

市などはクマ捕獲用の檻で出入口をふさいで閉じ込めており、半径およそ60メートルで屋内退避を呼びかけています。

舞鶴市が撮影した映像では、建物からクマが顔を出す様子が確認できます。

麻酔業者などが到着次第、通行規制を行って麻酔銃による緊急銃猟を実施する方針で、市や警察、京都府の職員が現場で安全確保にあたっています。  

京都府によりますと、緊急銃猟が実施されれば京都府内では初めてだということです。

　ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパンを訪れた2人。「十数年ぶり」だという大人気テーマパークで、三浦さんはスヌーピーの帽子をかぶり、ハリー・ポッターの世界観を再現したエリア「ウィザーディング・ワールド・オブ・ハリー・ポッター」では、名物ドリンク「バタービール」に舌鼓を打った。動画の最後では、「楽しかったね」とお互い言い合っていた。

articles.content: The new iPhone Handoff feature in iOS 27 allows users to utilise a single phone number across two different iPhones seamlessly. This innovation addresses a common inconvenience experienced by smartphone users, eliminating the need for manual SIM card swaps, call forwarding, or acquiring a second cellular line.This feature was previewed during the WWDC 2026 keynote in June, although detailed information was not immediately provided. Recent updates from MacRumors have clarified how this feature will actually function, providing users with a clearer understanding of its implementation.Users can conveniently configure the iPhone Handoff feature via the Settings app, specifically within the Cellular menu. During the initial setup process, individuals will select one iPhone to serve as the primary device, while designating the other as a companion device. This setup is crucial for allowing users to switch between devices effortlessly while maintaining the same phone number.According to Apple, the primary eSIM profile remains linked to the main iPhone, whereas a companion eSIM will be created for the secondary device. This arrangement ensures that users can alternate between their two iPhones without any disruption in service or connectivity.Account management is centralised, meaning all cellular plans and settings are controlled through the main iPhone. Additionally, the location sharing feature automatically updates based on the device that is currently connected to the service, allowing contacts to accurately view the location of the active phone in the Find My application.For the iPhone Handoff feature to operate effectively, having iOS 27 installed on both devices will not be the sole requirement. The functionality appears to be significantly dependent on telecom carrier support, similar to how cellular provisioning functions with the Apple Watch. Early indications suggest that major carriers like T-Mobile in the United States and Deutsche Telekom in Germany may be among the first to endorse this feature.This advancement could benefit users who rely on secondary devices for activities such as exercise, travel, or outdoor tasks, as it offers a safer alternative to using high-end flagship phones in potentially hazardous environments. The feature is positioned as a major improvement for those who balance multiple devices in their daily lives.iOS 27 is anticipated to be released to the public later this month following a rigorous three-month beta testing phase. articles.title: Carrying two phones is hard, but iOS 27 has a solution Android ought to copy
articles.excerpt: iOS 27 will introduce iPhone Handoff to run two phones on one number. Here is why Google should bring this network feature to Android.
articles.content:

Sep 3, 2026 — 6:04 AM ET

  • Apple is introducing “iPhone Handoff” in iOS 27, allowing a single cellular plan and phone number to be shared between a primary iPhone and a secondary companion iPhone via dual eSIMs.
  • Unlike basic Continuity features that require Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, iPhone Handoff could potentially operate natively at the network level, keeping the companion device fully connected even when the main phone is switched off.
  • Android has no such feature in the works for network-level phone number sharing, and it needs to copy this to reduce multi-device friction across Android’s varied form factors and use cases, such as foldables, camera phones, gaming handhelds, tablets, and even laptops.

Most users carry only one phone in their pocket, and many even use two SIMs in the same phone to reduce how many phones they need to carry. That being said, there are a bunch of people (including us phone reviewers) who end up with two and sometimes even more phones in our pockets. Using the same phone number on these phones has been nearly impossible, and even handling two phones and switching between them is often a logistical nightmare by itself. With the iPhone Ultra foldable right around the corner, Apple might have a solution up its sleeve for this niche problem in the form of “iPhone Handoff,” and this is something that even Google should copy for Android.

iPhone Handoff: Phone number sharing between iPhones

iPhone Handoff was mentioned during WWDC 2026 on a slide listing a whole bunch of new features coming in iOS 27, but Apple didn’t share further details at the time. Now, MacRumors forum member pdfu spotted the feature in the latest iOS 27 beta 8 release, showcasing how Apple will soon allow users to seamlessly switch between two iPhones while sharing a single phone number and cellular plan across both devices.

iPhone Handoff will live in Settings > Cellular when it rolls out with iOS 27 stable, with the setup designating one iPhone as the main phone housing your primary eSIM, while a secondary companion iPhone receives an associated companion eSIM. Cellular settings remain centralized on the primary phone, while location sharing dynamically switches to whichever device is currently active.

While this feature is said to rely on carrier support (with T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom tipped to be early partners), it will seemingly eliminate the friction of manually swapping physical SIM/eSIMs or incurring duplicate carrier line fees just to carry a secondary or backup phone.

From the information available so far, iPhone Handoff appears to differ from Apple’s existing Continuity features, even if it becomes part of the broader umbrella when it is released.

Features like text message forwarding and FaceTime call relay only piggyback on an active host device over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. iPhone Handoff, by contrast, seems to operate natively at the network and eSIM level. If you leave your primary flagship phone switched off at home, your companion phone remains a fully standalone cellular device operating under your existing phone number.

How does this tie in with the iPhone Ultra launch, you ask? While the iPhone Ultra is expected to be impressive as Apple’s first foldable, it will still be a first-generation model for the company and may have caveats users might not expect from their primary iPhone (such as the absence of a good telephoto camera). Given the expectedly high price of the iPhone Ultra, it’s not far-fetched to imagine that these users may also keep an older iPhone flagship around as a spare phone. With the iPhone Handoff feature, Apple will enable these users to seamlessly switch between their phones, making the transition to a foldable experience much easier.

Google should also look to bring network handoff to Android

Network/SIM handoff may appear to be a niche feature on the surface, but to me, it makes a lot of sense on Android, especially given the diverse range of form factors for phones, tablets, and beyond.

For instance, users with the disposable income could realistically buy a camera-centric phone for regular use, but switch to a gaming phone for dedicated gaming nights or to a rugged phone for their adventure needs. You could even switch to a smaller flip phone for social evenings when you might be low on pocket space, and swap to a large foldable for your daily spreadsheet use.

Going beyond phones, imagine cellular-equipped Android gaming handhelds that could seamlessly take over from your phone, if you’re okay with getting interrupted with a call in the middle of your gaming session. It might even work out well if your secondary phone number could seamlessly hop between your tablet and your Googlebook, for instance, letting you get cellular data on whichever device you choose to carry for the occasion.

Depending on how it is implemented, it could also be helpful when you need to give your eSIM-equipped phone in for a repair and temporarily switch to a spare phone.

Of course, a lot of the specifics depend on how carriers play along. But if done well, this has the potential to make Android feel much more like a cohesive ecosystem — you pick up a device (phone, tablet, handheld, or laptop), and you’re good to go. With this, Android multi-device ownership could go from a headache to one of the platform’s biggest perks.
